mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision date reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during similar high-rate regimes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates softening labor market pressure and disinflation, which tends to boost equity valuations and drive positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month by > 10% AND CPIAUCSL < previous month by > 0.5%
regime_hint: labor market softening coupled with disinflation
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns under such conditions are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly retail sales (not in catalog, so skip) cannot be used; instead, a surge in industrial production (INDPRO) above 105 indicates strengthening supply-side demand which anticipates a 5-day forward return positive in a non-recessionary regime.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite INDPRO > 105 for 2 consecutive months (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below 100 over three months signals supply-side bottlenecks that raise uncertainty and compress near-term equity valuations, producing negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during such contractions are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS crosses above 1% from below, it triggers a risk-on sentiment that elevates S&P 20-day forward returns, especially in non-expansionary regimes.
candidate_trigger: 3-month MA of FEDFUNDS crosses above 1% from below
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not rise significantly after the trigger (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.5% and a rise in housing starts (not in catalog - so use HOUST instead) above 1,200 suggests labor market tightening and construction optimism, both of which are associated with positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.5% AND HOUST > 1200 for 2 consecutive months
regime_hint: labor market tightening and construction acceleration
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns under such conditions are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to hyperinflationary expectations (not directly observable but inferred from CPIAUCSL > 300) is associated with a sharp decline in S&P 20-day forward returns regardless of other signals.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during such episodes are not significantly lower than during stable inflation periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 4-week moving average of industrial production (INDPRO) remains below its 50th percentile for three consecutive months, it reflects persistent supply-side weakness that is associated with negative 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: 4-week MA of INDPRO < 50th percentile for 3 months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns during such periods are not statistically negative (p > 0.05).
